title: Evaluation of machine learning algorithms for predicting direct-acting antiviral treatment failure among patients with chronic hepatitis C infection.
summary: Registry models predict DAA failure among 6,525 treated HCV patients, with 308 failures and reported discrimination beyond logistic regression; this is a bounded retrospective clinical outcome result.
ai_technology: Methods train elastic net, random forest, gradient boosting and feed-forward neural-network models on HCV-TARGET treatment data.
organization: Department of Pharmaceutical Outcomes and Policy

evidence.tested: Results report 308 failures among 6,525 adults and C-statistics 0.72–0.75 for ML vs 0.51 logistic regression.
evidence.unknown: Registry outcome is DAA failure; retrospective prediction has modest discrimination and no prospective deployment result.
evidence.ai_role: Methods train elastic net, random forest, gradient boosting and feed-forward neural-network models on HCV-TARGET treatment data.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
